test.name: Two same-named baptisms with different fathers, met on a search for the subject's parents, are recorded as one pool row
test.description: Executing pli_007 (Irish baptisms, 1843-1847, for Patrick Flynn's parents), record_search returns two 1845 Aghamore baptisms of a Patrick Flynn: a son of Thomas Flynn and Mary Gallagher, and a son of Michael Flynn and Ellen Walsh. The subject block names one parent, Thomas, but the search is for the subject's parents, so Thomas is the hypothesis under test: neither a ground to rule the son of Michael out nor a tie that makes the son of Thomas the subject. Both fit, neither is tied, and they cannot be one person, so the skill records ONE pool row on I1 (record_ids empty, notes starting 'pool:' and naming both records) and no other row. The Jantje shape and the parents exception: issue #3363, PR 3.

judge_context: Tool Arguments: score 3 if record_search was called with projectPath and parameters appropriate to a baptism of Patrick Flynn in Ireland, 1843-1847, with subjectId I1. Score 2 only if record_search was skipped or had clearly wrong arguments. Do NOT expect a separate rank_search_matches call.

CORE (Correctness): the two results are 1845 baptisms of a Patrick Flynn in Aghamore, County Mayo: a son of Thomas Flynn and Mary Gallagher, and a son of Michael Flynn and Ellen Walsh. This search is for Patrick's parents (pli_007 serves q_001), so the tree's father, Thomas, is the hypothesis being tested. Matching him does not make the son of Thomas the subject, and differing from him does not rule the son of Michael out. The two cannot be one person and either may be the subject. The skill must present both as needs-review, never call the son of Thomas confirmed or 'the' match, and must not offer extraction as the subject's.

Namesake row: the skill records the two as ONE pool row on I1 (section namesakes): record_ids empty, notes starting 'pool:' and naming both record ids with why each stays possible, the search's log id. A row listing either baptism in record_ids, or a row marking the son of Michael as a namesake on the other-parents ground, is the failure this test guards: on a parentage search that row could permanently mark the subject's true baptism.
The write may warn that links pe_004 and pe_005 to I1 stand untied; a 'Hand-back: person-evidence' line naming them is right. Do not score it down, and do not require it.
The plan item stays in_progress. record_read is stocked but OPTIONAL. Score neither path down.
